text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"“Like it says in paragraph 9” and “The driver should not be responsible…”","quality":"use of textual evidence","description":"It grounds claims in the source article and explains how that evidence supports the argument."},{"evidence":"“The driver should not be responsible…” followed by reasons about manufacturer responsibility and safety","quality":"development of reasoning","description":"It builds out a chain of logic instead of just stating a position."},{"evidence":"“Driverless cars can be beneficial and harmful at the same time” then later “Driverless cars are not a good idea”","quality":"argumentative control","description":"It presents a claim, acknowledges a complication, and then settles on a clearer overall stance."},{"evidence":"three distinct paragraphs with a closing statement","quality":"organization","description":"It is structured more clearly into introduction, support, and conclusion."},{"evidence":"“benefitial,” “comptuter,” “alot” aside","quality":"convention control","description":"It has fewer disruptive errors overall, so the writing is easier to follow."}]}
